correctness.rationale: The source supplies the exact ingredients: logarithmic convexity of the spherical mean and convergence of its quotient by log radius to the Lelong number. For the convex function phi(x)=S(u,e^x), every fixed backward increment tends to the asymptotic slope times its length. A finite one-sided slope at a fixed x0 bounds all such increments by C s for x<=x0. The finite logarithmic radius moment therefore gives an integrable majorant, so dominated convergence proves the arbitrary-kernel identity. The radial mollifier and uniform-ball constants are exact pushforward computations.

value.rationale: The fresh source presents the exact coefficient 1/(2n) as its main additive refinement of classical quotient asymptotics and separately introduces radial regularizations. The accepted result unifies these two parts: every radial kernel has an exact coefficient equal to its logarithmic radius moment, and any smooth radial mollifier recovers the Lelong number additively. This is a natural structural extension of the source's main theorem and gives a reusable comparison calculus for regularization kernels rather than an arbitrary special case.
